alloxanate: A combination of alloxanic acid and a base or base or positive radical.
alcoholometric: Relating to the alcoholometer or alcoholometry. The alcoholometrical strength of spirituous liquors. Ure.
alvine: Of, from, in, or pertaining to, the belly or the intestines; as, alvine discharges; alvine concretions.
almoner: One who distributes alms, esp. the doles and alms of religious houses, almshouses, etc.; also, one who dispenses alms for another, as the almoner of a prince, bishop, etc.
allottee: One to whom anything is allotted; one to whom an allotment is made.
aloofness: State of being aloof. Rogers (1642). The . . . aloofness of his dim forest life. Thoreau.
alalia: Inability to utter articulate sounds, due either to paralysis of the larynx or to that form of aphasia, called motor, or ataxis, aphasia, due to loss of control of the muscles of speech.
alnager: A measure by the ell; formerly a sworn officer in England, whose duty was to inspect act measure woolen cloth, and fix upon it a seal.
alienist: One who treats diseases of the mind. Ed. Rev.
albinism: The state or condition of being an albino: abinoism; leucopathy.
alarm: 1. A summons to arms, as on the approach of an enemy. Arming to answer in a night alarm. Shak. 2. Any sound or information intended to give notice of approaching danger; | 1. alternator: An electric generator or dynamo for producing alternating currents.
alcoholometrical: Relating to the alcoholometer or alcoholometry. The alcoholometrical strength of spirituous liquors. Ure.
alexipyretic: Serving to drive off fever; antifebrile. -- n. A febrifuge.
alineeation: Alignment; position in a straight line, as of two planets with the sun. Whewell. The allineation of the two planets. C. A. Young.
allemande: 1. (Mus.) A dance in moderate twofold time, invented by the French in the reign of Louis XIV.; -- now mostly found in suites of pieces, like those of Bach and Handel. 2. A figure in dancing.
alumstone: A subsulphate of alumina and potash; alunite.
altimetry: The art of measuring altitudes, or heights.
alternativeness: The quality of being alternative, or of offering a choice between two.
altarage: 1. The offerings made upon the altar, or to a church. 2. The profit which accrues to the priest, by reason of the altar, from the small tithes. Shipley.
alleluiah: An exclamation signifying Praise ye Jehovah. Hence: A song of praise to God. See Hallelujah, the commoner form. I heard a great voice of much people in heaven, saying, Alleluia. Rev. xix. 1.
albertite: A bituminous mineral resembling asphaltum, found in the county of A.
almadie: (a) A bark canoe used by the Africans. (b) A boat used at Calicut, in India, about eighty feet long, and six or seven broad.
alchemist: One who practices alchemy. You are alchemist; make gold. Shak.
allumette: A match for lighting candles, lamps, etc.
alterative: Causing ateration. Specifically: Gradually changing, or tending to change, a morbid state of the functions into one of health. Burton. | A medicine or treatment which gradually induces a change, and restores healthy functions without sensible evacuations.
alloxantin: A substance produced by acting upon uric with warm and very dilute nitric acid.
alcyonium: A genus of fleshy Alcyonaria, its polyps somewhat resembling flowers with eight fringed rays. The term was also formerly used for certain species of sponges.
aladinist: One of a sect of freethinkers among the Mohammedans.
albuminin: The substance of the cells which inclose the white of birds' eggs.
alveated: Formed or vaulted like a beehive.
alimentariness: The quality of being alimentary; nourishing quality.
alkaloid: An organic base, especially one of a class of substances occurring ready formed in the tissues of plants and the bodies of animals. Note: Alcaloids all contain nitrogen, carbon, and hydrogen, and… | Pertaining to, resembling, or containing, alkali.
alguazil: An inferior officer of justice in Spain; a warrant officer; a constable. Prescott.
algometer: An instrument for measuring sensations of pain due to pressure. It has a piston rod with a blunted tip which is pressed against the skin. -- Al*gom"e*try (#), n. -- Al`go*met"ric (#), *met"ric*al (#), a. --Al`go*met"ric*al*ly, adv.
algaroth: A term used for the Powder of Algaroth, a white powder which is a compound of trichloride and trioxide of antimony. It was formerly used in medicine as an emetic, purgative, and diaphoretic.
allantoin: A crystalline, transparent, colorless substance found in the allantoic liquid of the fetal calf; -- formerly called allantoic acid and amniotic acid.
alveary: 1. A beehive, or something resembling a beehive. Barret. 2. (Anat.) The hollow of the external ear. Quincy.
alizari: The madder of the Levant. Brande & C.
altarwise: In the proper position of an altar, that is, at the east of a church with its ends towards the north and south. Shipley.

alkalization: The act rendering alkaline by impregnating with an alkali; a conferring of alkaline qualities.
almsfolk: Persons supported by alms; almsmen. (old) Holinshed.
alexandrine: Belonging to Alexandria; Alexandrian. Bancroft. | A kind of verse consisting in English of twelve syllables. The needless Alexandrine ends the song, That, like a wounded snake, drags its slow length along. Pope.
alectorides: A group of birds including the common fowl and the pheasants.
alchemize: To change by alchemy; to transmute. Lovelace.
altarist: (a) A chaplain. (b) A vicar of a church.
aldermanlike: Like or suited to an alderman.
alkalamide: One of a series of compounds that may be regarded as ammonia in which a part of the hydrogen has been replaced by basic, and another part by acid, atoms or radicals.
almain: 1. A German. Also adj., German. Shak. 2. The German language. J. Foxe. 3. A kind of dance. See Allemande. Almain rivets, Almayne rivets, or Alman rivets, a sort of light armor from Germany, characterized by overlapping plates, arranged to slide on rivets, and thus afford great flexibility.
aline: To range or place in a line; to bring into line; to align. Evelyn.

almondfurnace: A kind of furnace used in refining, to separate the metal from cinders and other foreign matter. Chambers.
alkahest: The fabled "universal solvent" of the alchemists; a menstruum capable of dissolving all bodies. -- Al`ka*hes"tic, a.
algerine: Of or pertaining to Algiers or Algeria. | A native or one of the people of Algiers or Algeria. Also, a pirate.
alluring: That allures; attracting; charming; tempting. -- Al*lur"ing*ly, adv. -- Al*lur"ing*ness, n.
alphabetics: The science of representing spoken sounds by letters.
alphabet: 1. The letters of a language arranged in the customary order; the series of letters or signs which form the elements of written language. 2. The simplest rudiments; elements. | To designate by the letters of the alphabet; to arrange alphabetically.
althorn: An instrument of the saxhorn family, used exclusively in military music, often replacing the French horn. Grove.
allhallowtide: The time at or near All Saints, or November 1st.
altocumulus: A fleecy cloud formation consisting of large whitish or grayish globular cloudlets with shaded portions, often grouped in flocks or rows.
alife: On my life; dearly. (old) "I love that sport alife." Beau. & Fl.
alecost: The plant costmary, which was formerly much used for flavoring ale.
aleutic: Of or pertaining to a chain of islands between Alaska and Kamtchatka; also, designating these islands.
alatern: An ornamental evergreen shrub (Rhamnus alaternus) belonging to the buckthorns.
almagest: The celebrated work of Ptolemy of Alexandria, which contains nearly all that is known of the astronomical observations and theories of the ancients. The name was extended to other similar works.
alternately: 1. In reciprocal succession; succeeding by turns; in alternate order. 2. (Math.) By alternation; when, in a proportion, the antecedent term is compared with antecedent, and consequent.
allspice: The berry of the pimento (Eugenia pimenta), a tree of the West Indies; a spice of a mildly pungent taste, and agreeably aromatic; Jamaica pepper; pimento. alloyage: The act or art of alloying metals; also, the combination or alloy.
alembroth: The salt of wisdom of the alchemists, a double salt composed of the chlorides of ammonium and mercury. It was formerly used as a stimulant. Brande & C.
allegheny: 1. Of or pertaining to the Allegheny Mountains, or the region where they are situated. Also Al"le*gha`ny. 2. [From the Allegheny River, Pennsylvania.] (Geol.) Pertaining to or designating a subdivision of the Pennsylvanian coal measure.
alphol: A crystalline derivative of salicylic acid, used as an antiseptic and antirheumatic.
alexiterical: Resisting poison; obviating the effects of venom; alexipharmic.
alogian: One of an ancient sect who rejected St. John's Gospel and the Apocalypse, which speak of Christ as the Logos. Shipley.
algebraize: To perform by algebra; to reduce to algebraic form.

alkaloidal: Pertaining to, resembling, or containing, alkali.
album: 1. (Rom. Antiq.) A white tablet on which anything was inscribed, as a list of names, etc. 2. A register for visitors' names; a visitors' book. 3. A blank book, in which to insert autographs sketches, memorial writing of friends, photographs, etc.
aldehydic: Of or pertaining to aldehyde; as, aldehydic acid. Miller.
allfours: All four legs of a quadruped; or the two legs and two arms of a person. "No simile can go on all fours." Macaulay.
algates: 1. Always; wholly; everywhere. (old) Ulna now he algates must forego. Spenser. Note: Still used in the north of England in the sense of "everywhere." 2. By any or means; at all events. (old) Fairfax. 3. Notwithstanding; yet. (old) Chaucer.
allegoric: Belonging to, or consisting of, allegory; of the nature of an allegory; describing by resemblances; figurative. "An allegoric tale." Falconer. "An allegorical application." Pope. Allegorical being . . . that kind of language which says one thing, but means another. Max Miller. Al`le*gor"ic*al*ly, adv. -- Al`le*gor"ic*al*ness, n.
aleurone: An albuminoid substance which occurs in minute grains ("protein granules") in maturing seeds and tubers; -- supposed to be a modification of protoplasm.
alongside: Along or by the side; side by side with; -- often with of; as, bring the boat alongside; alongside of him; alongside of the tree.
aland: On land; to the land; ashore. "Cast aland." Sir P. Sidney.
almeh: An Egyptian dancing girl; an Alma. The Almehs lift their arms in dance. Bayard Taylor.
alcoranist: One who adheres to the letter of the Koran, rejecting all traditions.
alderman: 1. A senior or superior; a person of rank or dignity. allonym: 1. The name of another person assumed by the author of a work. 2. A work published under the name of some one other than the author.
alkalescence: A tendency to become alkaline; or the state of a substance in which alkaline properties begin to be developed, or to predominant. Ure.
aldine: An epithet applied to editions (chiefly of the classics) which proceeded from the press of Aldus Manitius, and his family, of Venice, for the most part in the 16th century and known by the sign of the anchor and the dolphin. alibi: The plea or mode of defense under which a person on trial for a crime proves or attempts to prove that he was in another place when the alleged act was committed; as, to set up an alibi; to prove an alibi.
alone: 1. Quite by one's self; apart from, or exclusive of, others; single; solitary; -- applied to a person or thing. Alone on a wide, wide sea. Coleridge. Luke iv. 4.
allegorist: One who allegorizes; a writer of allegory. Hume.
altruism: Regard for others, both natural and moral; devotion to the interests of others; brotherly kindness; -- opposed to egoism or selfishness. [Recent] J. S. Mill.
alternative: 1. Offering a choice of two things. 2. Disjunctive; as, an alternative conjunction. 3. Alternate; reciprocal. (old) Holland. | 1. alkarsin: A spontaneously inflammable liquid, having a repulsive odor, and consisting of cacodyl and its oxidation products; -- called also Cadel's fuming liquid.
aldermanry: 1. The district or ward of an alderman. 2. The office or rank of an alderman. B. Jonson.
aleberry: A beverage, formerly made by boiling ale with spice, sugar, and sops of bread. Their aleberries, caudles, possets. Beau. & Fl.
alburnum: The white and softer part of wood, between the inner bark and the hard wood or duramen; sapwood.
alated: Winged; having wings, or side appendages like wings.

alienor: One who alienates or transfers property to another. Blackstone.

algology: The study or science of algæ or seaweeds.
alferes: An ensign; a standard bearer. (old) J. Fletcher.
alternat: A usage, among diplomats, of rotation in precedence among representatives of equal rank, sometimes determined by lot and at other times in regular order. The practice obtains in the signing of treaties and conventions between nations.
aleatory: Depending on some uncertain contingency; as, an aleatory contract. Bouvier.
alkalify: To convert into an alkali; to give alkaline properties to. | To become changed into an alkali.
alternatingcurrent: A current which periodically changes or reverses its direction of flow.
allodial: Pertaining to allodium; freehold; free of rent or service; held independent of a lord paramount; -- opposed to feudal; as, allodial lands; allodial system. Blackstone. | Anything held allodially. W. Coxe.
algarot: A term used for the Powder of Algaroth, a white powder which is a compound of trichloride and trioxide of antimony. It was formerly used in medicine as an emetic, purgative, and diaphoretic.
alomancy: Divination by means of salt. [Spelt also halomancy.] Morin.
altissimo: The part or notes situated above F in alt.
aliquant: An aliquant part of a number or quantity is one which does not divide it without leaving a remainder; thus, 5 is an aliquant part of 16. Opposed to aliquot.

alizarin: A coloring principle, C14H6O2(OH)2, found in madder, and now produced artificially from anthracene. It produces the Turkish reds.
alienable: Capable of being alienated, sold, or transferred to another; as, land is alienable according to the laws of the state.
allegretto: Quicker than andante, but not so quick as allegro. -- n. A movement in this time.
allomorph: (a) Any one of two or more distinct crystalline forms of the same substance; or the substance having such forms; -- as, carbonate of lime occurs in the allomorphs calcite and aragonite. alluvion: 1. Wash or flow of water against the shore or bank. 2. An overflowing; an inundation; a flood. Lyell. 3. Matter deposited by an inundation or the action of flowing water; alluvium.

alcyonaria: One of the orders of Anthozoa. It includes the Alcyonacea, Pennatulacea, and Gorgonacea.
alkaline: Of or pertaining to an alkali or to alkalies; having the properties of an alkali. alfilaria: The pin grass (Erodium cicutarium), a weed in California.
aleppograss: One of the cultivated forms of Andropogon Halepensis (syn. Sorghum Halepense). See Andropogon, below.
almucantar: A small circle of the sphere parallel to the horizon; a circle or parallel of altitude. Two stars which have the same almucantar have the same altitude. See Almacantar.
allay: 1. To make quiet or put at rest; to pacify or appease; to quell; to calm; as, to allay popular excitement; to allay the tumult of the passions. 2. To alleviate; to abate; to mitigate; | To diminish in strength; to abate; to subside. "When the rage allays." Shak.
aliseptal: Relating to expansions of the nasal septum.
alleluia: An exclamation signifying Praise ye Jehovah. Hence: A song of praise to God. See Hallelujah, the commoner form. I heard a great voice of much people in heaven, saying, Alleluia. Rev. xix. 1.

alcoholmetrical: Relating to the alcoholometer or alcoholometry. The alcoholometrical strength of spirituous liquors. Ure.
allure: To attempt to draw; to tempt by a lure or bait, that is, by the offer of some good, real or apparent; to invite by something flattering or acceptable; to entice; to attract. | Gait; bearing. The swing, the gait, the pose, the allure of these men. Harper's Mag.
alebench: A bench in or before an alehouse. Bunyan.
alterableness: The quality of being alterable; variableness; alterability.
alutaceous: 1. Leathery. 2. Of a pale brown color; leather-yellow. Brande.
alco: A small South American dog, domesticated by the aborigines.
allyl: An organic radical, C3H5, existing especially in oils of garlic and mustard.
alar: 1. Pertaining to, or having, wings. 2. (Bot.) Axillary; in the fork or axil. Gray.
algebra: 1. (Math.) That branch of mathematics which treats of the relations and properties of quantity by means of letters and other symbols. It is applicable to those relations that are true of every kind of magnitude. 2. A treatise on this science.
allophylian: Pertaining to a race or a language neither Aryan nor Semitic. J. Prichard.

allantoidal: Of or pertaining to the allantois.
almsdeed: An act of charity. Acts ix. 36.

aldermanship: The condition, position, or office of an alderman. Fabyan.
albertware: A soft ornamental terra-cotta pottery, sold in the biscuit state for decorating.
allusive: 1. Figurative; symbolical. 2. Having reference to something not fully expressed; containing an allusion.

alphabetism: The expression of spoken sounds by an alphabet. Encyc. Brit.
algerian: Of or pertaining to Algeria. -- n. A native of Algeria.

alinasal: Pertaining to expansions of the nasal bone or cartilage.

along: 1. By the length; in a line with the length; lengthwise. Some laid along . . . on spokes of wheels are hung. Dryden. 2. altho: Although. [Reformed spelling] Alt"horn`, n. Etym: [Alt + horn.] (Mus.) An instrument of the saxhorn family, used exclusively in military music, often replacing the French horn. Grove.
allhallown: Of or pertaining to the time of Allhallows. (old) "Allhallown summer." Shak. (i. e., late summer; "Indian Summer").
alertness: The quality of being alert or on the alert; briskness; nimbleness; activity.

alpenstock: A long staff, pointed with iron, used in climbing the Alps. Cheever.
alcyonoid: Like or pertaining to the Alcyonaria. -- n. A zoöphyte of the order Alcyonaria.

aludel: One of the pear-shaped pots open at both ends, and so formed as to be fitted together, the neck of one into the bottom of another in succession; -- used in the process of sublimation. Ure.
allot: 1. To distribute by lot. 2. aluminic: Of or containing aluminium; as, aluminic phosphate.

allecret: A kind of light armor used in the sixteenth century, esp. by the Swiss. Fairholt.
alveoliform: Having the form of alveoli, or little sockets, cells, or cavities.

alack: An exclamation expressive of sorrow. [Archaic. or Poet.] Shak.

alure: A walk or passage; -- applied to passages of various kinds. The sides of every street were covered with fresh alures of marble. T. Warton.

allocate: 1. To distribute or assign; to allot. Burke. 2. To localize.

algologist: One learned about algæ; a student of algology.
alamodality: The quality of being à la mode; conformity to the mode or fashion; fashionableness. Southey.
aloof: 1. At or from a distance, but within view, or at a small distance; apart; away. Our palace stood aloof from streets. Dryden. 2. Without sympathy; unfavorably. To make the Bible as from the hand of… | Away from; clear from. (old) Rivetus . . . would fain work himself aloof these rocks and quicksands. Milton.
altitude: 1. Space extended upward; height; the perpendicular elevation of an object above its foundation, above the ground, or above a given level, or of one object above another; as, the altitude of a mountain, or of a bird above the top of a tree. 2.
alpha: The first letter in the Greek alphabet, answering to A, and hence used to denote the beginning. In am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last. Rev. xxii. 13. Note: Formerly used also denote the chief; as, Plato was the alpha of the wits. Note: In cataloguing stars, the brightest star of a constellation in designated by Alpha (a); as, a Lyræ.
alkaliwaste: Waste material from the manufacture of alkali; specif., soda waste.
allotrophic: (a) (Physiol.) Changed or modified in nutritive power by the process of digestion. (b) (Plant Physiol.) Dependent upon other organisms for nutrition; heterotrophic; -- said of plants unable to perform photosynthesis, as all saprophytes; -- opposed to autotrophic.
albification: The act or process of making white. (old)
alpenhorn: A curved wooden horn about three feet long, with a cupped mouthpiece and a bell, used by the Swiss to sound the ranz des vaches and other melodies. Its notes are open harmonics of the tube.
alcyonic: Of or pertaining to the Alcyonaria.
alchemistical: Relating to or practicing alchemy. Metaphysical and alchemistical legislators. Burke.
albumin: A thick, viscous nitrogenous substance, which is the chief and characteristic constituent of white of eggs and of the serum of blood, and is found in other animal substances, both fluid and solid, also in many plants. It is soluble in water is coagulated by heat ad by certain chemical reagents. Acid albumin, a modification of albumin produced by the action of dilute acids.
aluminize: To treat impregnate with alum; to alum.
albe: Although; albeit. (old) Albe Clarissa were their chiefest founderess. Spenser.
alhambresque: Made or decorated after the fanciful style of the ornamentation in the Alhambra, which affords an unusually fine exhibition of Saracenic or Arabesque architecture.
albuminimeter: An instrument for ascertaining the quantity of albumen in a liquid.
already: Prior to some specified time, either past, present, or future; by this time; previously. "Joseph was in Egypt already." Exod. i. 5. I say unto you, that Elias is come already. Matt. xvii. 12. Note: It has reference to past time, but may be used for a future past; as, when you shall arrive, the business will be already completed, or will have been already completed.
alluminor: An illuminator of manuscripts and books; a limner. (old) Cowell.
alsike: A species of clover with pinkish or white flowers; Trifolium hybridum.
alliance: 1. The state of being allied; the act of allying or uniting; a union or connection of interests between families, states, parties, etc., especially between families by marriage and states by compact,… | To connect by alliance; to ally. (old)
alliterative: Pertaining to, or characterized by, alliteration; as, alliterative poetry. -- Al*lit"er*a*tive*ly, adv. -- Al*lit"er*a*tive*ness, n.
aleconner: Orig., an officer appointed to look to the goodness of ale and beer; also, one of the officers chosen by the liverymen of London to inspect the measures used in public houses. But the office is a sinecure. [Also called aletaster.] [Eng.]
alkermes: A compound cordial, in the form of a confection, deriving its name from the kermes insect, its principal ingredient.
altogether: 1. All together; conjointly. (old) Altogether they wenChaucer. 2. Without exception; wholly; completely. Every man at his best state is altogether vanity. Ps. xxxix. 5.
albuminose: A diffusible substance formed from albumin by the action of natural or artificial gastric juice. See Peptone. | Pertaining to, or containing, albumen; having the properties of, or resembling, albumen or albumin. -- Al*bu"mi*nous*ness, n.
alphabetarian: A learner of the alphabet; an abecedarian. Abp. Sancroft.
allantoic: Pertaining to, or contained in, the allantois. Allantoic acid. (Chem.) See Allantoin.
alcoranic: Of or pertaining to the Koran.
alimentally: So as to serve for nourishment or food; nourishing quality. Sir T. Browne.
alleghany: 1. Of or pertaining to the Allegheny Mountains, or the region where they are situated. Also Al"le*gha`ny. 2. [From the Allegheny River, Pennsylvania.] (Geol.) Pertaining to or designating a subdivision of the Pennsylvanian coal measure.
aloft: 1. On high; in the air; high above the ground. "He steers his flight aloft." Milton. 2. (Naut.) In the top; at the mast head, or on the higher yards or rigging; overhead; hence (Fig. | Above; on top of. (old) Fresh waters run aloft the sea. Holland.
alloo: To incite dogs by a call; to halloo. (old)
allotheism: The worship of strange gods. Jer. Taylor.
aliethmoidal: Pertaining to expansions of the ethmoid bone or
alem: The imperial standard of the Turkish Empire.
aleppobutton: A chronic skin affection terminating in an ulcer, most commonly of the face. It is endemic along the Mediterranean, and is probably due to a specific bacillus. Called also Aleppo ulcer, Biskara boil, Delhi boil, Oriental sore, etc.
alfa: A plant (Macrochloa tenacissima) of North Africa; also, its fiber, used in paper making.
alacrity: A cheerful readiness, willingness, or promptitude; joyous activity; briskness; sprightliness; as, the soldiers advanced with alacrity to meet the enemy. I have not that alacrity of spirit, Nor cheer of mind that I was wont to have. Shak.
alepole: A pole set up as the sign of an alehouse. (old)
alloy: 1. Any combination or compound of metals fused together; a mixture of metals; for example, brass, which is an alloy of copper and zinc. But when mercury is one of the metals, the compound is called… | 1. alienee: One to whom the title of property is transferred; -- opposed to alienor. It the alienee enters and keeps possession. Blackstone.
aloud: With a loud voice, or great noise; loudly; audibly. Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice. Isa. lviii. 1.
albication: The process of becoming white, or developing white patches, or streaks.
all: 1. The whole quantity, extent, duration, amount, quality, or degree of; the whole; the whole number of; any whatever; every; as, all the wheat; all the land; all the year; all the strength; | 1. Wholly; completely; altogether; entirely; quite; very; as, all bedewed; my friend is all for amusement. "And cheeks all pale." Byron. Note: In the ancient phrases, all too dear, all too much, all…
aliunde: From another source; from elsewhere; as, a case proved aliunde; evidence aliunde.
aliturgical: Applied to those days when the holy sacrifice is not offered. Shipley.
allantois: A membranous appendage of the embryos of mammals, birds, and reptiles, -- in mammals serving to connect the fetus with the parent; the urinary vesicle.
alunogen: A white fibrous mineral frequently found on the walls of mines and quarries, chiefly hydrous sulphate of alumina; -- also called feather alum, and hair salt.
alewife: A woman who keeps an alehouse. Gay. | A North American fish (Clupea vernalis) of the Herring family. It is called also ellwife, ellwhop, branch herring. The name is locally applied to other related species.
allocution: 1. The act or manner of speaking to, or of addressing in words. 2. An address; a hortatory or authoritative address as of a pope to his clergy. Addison.
alienism: 1. The status or legal condition of an alien; alienage. The law was very gentle in the construction of the disability of alienism. Kent. 2. The study or treatment of diseases of the mind.
allegorize: 1. To form or turn into allegory; as, to allegorize the history of a people. 2. To treat as allegorical; to understand in an allegorical sense; as, when a passage in a writer may understood literally or figuratively, he who gives it a figurative sense is said to allegorize it.
almayne: 1. A German. Also adj., German. Shak. 2. The German language. J. Foxe. 3. A kind of dance. See Allemande. Almain rivets, Almayne rivets, or Alman rivets, a sort of light armor from Germany, characterized by overlapping plates, arranged to slide on rivets, and thus afford great flexibility.
alutation: The tanning or dressing of leather. (old) Blount.
alphitomancy: Divination by means of barley meal. Knowles.
algaroba: (a) The Carob, a leguminous tree of the Mediterranean region; also, its edible beans or pods, called St. John's bread. (b) The Honey mesquite (Prosopis juliflora), a small tree found from California to Buenos Ayres; also, its sweet, pulpy pods. A valuable gum, resembling gum arabic, is collected from the tree in Texas and Mexico.
alpist: The seed of canary grass (Phalaris Canariensis), used for feeding cage birds.
althea: (a) A genus of plants of the Mallow family. It includes the officinal marsh mallow, and the garden hollyhocks. (b) An ornamental shrub (Hibiscus Syriacus) of the Mallow family.
algid: Cold; chilly. Bailey. Algid cholera (Med.), Asiatic cholera.
albuminosis: A morbid condition due to excessive increase of albuminous elements in the blood.
almacantar: (a) Same as Almucantar. (b) A recently invented instrument for observing the heavenly bodies as they cross a given almacantar circle. See Almucantar.
aloin: A bitter purgative principle in aloes.
alquifou: A lead ore found in Cornwall, England, and used by potters to give a green glaze to their wares; potter's ore.
alcornoque: The bark of several trees, esp. of Bowdichia virgilioides of Brazil, used as a remedy for consumption; of Byrsonima crassifolia, used in tanning; of Alchornea latifolia, used medicinally; or of Quercus ilex, the cork tree.
alligate: To tie; to unite by some tie. Instincts alligated to their nature. Sir M. Hale.
allegeable: Capable of being alleged or affirmed. The most authentic examples allegeable in the case. South.
allonge: 1. (Fencing) A thrust or pass; a lunge. 2. A slip of paper attached to a bill of exchange for receiving indorsements, when the back of the bill itself is already full; a rider. | To thrust with a sword; to lunge.
allium: A genus of plants, including the onion, garlic, leek, chive, etc.
albumgraecum: Dung of dogs or hyenas, which becomes white by exposure to air. It is used in dressing leather, and was formerly used in medicine.
alburn: The bleak, a small European fish having scales of a peculiarly silvery color which are used in making artificial pearls.
aldermanic: Relating to, becoming to, or like, an alderman; characteristic of an alderman.
allopathist: One who practices allopathy; one who professes allopathy.
allegation: 1. The act of alleging or positively asserting. 2. That which is alleged, asserted, or declared; positive assertion; formal averment I thought their allegation but reasonable. Steele. 3. (Law) A statement by a party of what he undertakes to prove, -- usually applied to each separate averment; the charge or matter undertaken to be proved.
algous: Of or pertaining to the algæ, or seaweeds; abounding with, or like, seaweed.
alveus: The channel of a river. Weate.
alkalimetry: The art or process of ascertaining the strength of alkalies, or the quantity present in alkaline mixtures.
alley: 1. A narrow passage; especially a walk or passage in a garden or park, bordered by rows of trees or bushes; a bordered way. I know each lane and every alley green. Milton. 2. | A choice taw or marble. Dickens.
albata: A white metallic alloy; which is made into spoons, forks, teapots, etc. British plate or German silver. See German silver, under German.
allotropic: Of or pertaining to allotropism. -- Al`lo*trop"ic*al*ly, adv. Allotropic state, the several conditions which occur in a case of allotropism.
alternatively: In the manner of alternatives, or that admits the choice of one out of two things.
also: 1. In like manner; likewise. (old) 2. In addition; besides; as well; further; too. Lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven . . . for where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. Matt. vi. 20. 3. Even as; as; so. (old) Chaucer. Syn. -- Also, Likewise, Too. These words are used by way of transition, in leaving one thought and passing to another.
aldermanity: 1. Aldermen collectively; the body of aldermen. 2. The state of being an alderman. [Jocular]
alteration: 1. The act of altering or making different. Alteration, though it be from worse to better, hath in it incoveniences. Hooker. 2. The state of being altered; a change made in the form or nature of a thing; changed condition. Ere long might perceive Strange alteration in me. Milton. Appius Claudius admitted to the senate the sons of those who had been slaves;
allegorizer: One who allegorizes, or turns things into allegory; an allegorist.
alonely: Only; merely; singly. (old) This said spirit was not given alonely unto him, but unto all his heirs and posterity. Latimer.
allhallows: 1. All the saints (in heaven). (old) 2. All Saints' Day, November 1st. (old)
algoid: Of the nature of, or resembling, an alga.
alliterate: To employ or place so as to make alliteration. Skeat. | To compose alliteratively; also, to constitute alliteration.
algate: 1. Always; wholly; everywhere. (old) Ulna now he algates must forego. Spenser. Note: Still used in the north of England in the sense of "everywhere." 2. By any or means; at all events. (old) Fairfax. 3. Notwithstanding; yet. (old) Chaucer.
alike: Having resemblance or similitude; similar; without difference. [Now used only predicatively.] The darkness and the light are both alike to thee. Ps. cxxxix. 12. | In the same manner, form, or degree; in common; equally; as, we are all alike concerne.
almug: A tree or wood of the Bible (2 Chron. ii. 8; 1 K. x. 11). Note: Most writers at the present day follow Celsius, who takes it to be the red sandalwood of China and the Indian Archipelago. W. Smith.
allurer: One who, or that which, allures.
alarum: See Alarm. [Now Poetic] Note: The variant form alarum is now commonly restricted to an alarm signal or the mechanism to sound an alarm (as in an alarm clock.)
aldol: A colorless liquid, C4H8O2, obtained by condensation of two molecules of acetaldehyde: CH3CHO + CH3CHO = H3CH(OH)CH2CO; also, any of various derivatives of this. The same reaction has been applied, under the name of aldol condensation, to the production of many compounds.
alinement: Same as Alignment. Note: [The Eng. form alinement is preferable to alignment, a bad spelling of the French]. New Eng. Dict. (Murray).
altiscope: An arrangement of lenses and mirrors which enables a person to see an object in spite of intervening objects.
algin: A nitrogenous substance resembling gelatin, obtained from certain algæ.
albuminous: Pertaining to, or containing, albumen; having the properties of, or resembling, albumen or albumin. -- Al*bu"mi*nous*ness, n.
alert: 1. Watchful; vigilant; active in vigilance. 2. Brisk; nimble; moving with celerity. An alert young fellow. Addison. Syn. -- Active; agile; lively; quick; prompt. | An alarm from a real or threatened attack; a sudden attack; also, a bugle sound to give warning. "We have had an alert." Farrow. On the alert, on the lookout or watch against attack or danger;
almuce: Same as Amice, a hood or cape.
altitudinal: Of or pertaining to height; as, altitudinal measurements.
alcyonacea: A group of soft-bodied Alcyonaria, of which Alcyonium is the type. See Illust. under Alcyonaria.
alledge: See Allege. (old) Note: This spelling, corresponding to abridge, was once the prevailing one.
alleviative: Tending to alleviate. -- n. That which alleviates.
almude: A measure for liquids in several countries. In Portugal the Lisbon almude is about 4.4, and the Oporto almude about 6.6, gallons U. S. measure. In Turkey the "almud" is about 1.4 gallons.
allegro: Brisk, lively. -- n. An allegro movement; a quick, sprightly strain or piece.
alacrify: To rouse to action; to inspirit.
almond: 1. The fruit of the almond tree. Note: The different kinds, as bitter, sweet, thin-shelled, thick- shelled almonds, and Jordan almonds, are the products of different varieties of the one species, Amygdalus communis, a native of the Mediterranean region and western Asia. 2. The tree bears the fruit; almond tree. 3. Anything shaped like an almond.
allopathically: In a manner conformable to allopathy; by allopathic methods.
allodium: Freehold estate; land which is the absolute property of the owner; real estate held in absolute independence, without being subject to any rent, service, or acknowledgment to a superior. It is thus opposed to feud. Blackstone. Bouvier.
almonry: The place where an almoner resides, or where alms are distributed.
alman: 1. A German. Also adj., German. Shak. 2. The German language. J. Foxe. 3. A kind of dance. See Allemande. Almain rivets, Almayne rivets, or Alman rivets, a sort of light armor from Germany, characterized by overlapping plates, arranged to slide on rivets, and thus afford great flexibility.
alphabetically: In an alphabetic manner; in the customary order of the letters.
alumroot: A North American herb (Heuchera Americana) of the Saxifrage family, whose root has astringent properties.
altercation: Warm contention in words; dispute carried on with heat or anger; controversy; wrangle; wordy contest. "Stormy altercations." Macaulay. Syn. -- Altercation, Dispute, Wrangle. The term dispute is in most cases, but not necessarily, applied to a verbal contest; as, a dispute on the lawfulness of war.
alpen: Of or pertaining to the Alps. "The Alpen snow." J. Fletcher.
allude: To refer to something indirectly or by suggestion; to have reference to a subject not specifically and plainly mentioned; -- followed by to; as, the story alludes to a recent transaction. | To compare allusively; to refer (something) as applicable. (old) Wither.
aloneness: A state of being alone, or without company; solitariness. Bp. Montagu.
allotriophagy: A depraved appetite; a desire for improper food.
alphabetic: 1. Pertaining to, furnished with, expressed by, or in the order of, the letters of the alphabet; as, alphabetic characters, writing, languages, arrangement. 2. Literal. (old) "Alphabetical servility." Milton.
alienation: 1. The act of alienating, or the state of being alienated. 2. (Law) A transfer of title, or a legal conveyance of property to another. 3. al: All; wholly; completely; as, almighty,almost. (b) Etym: [L. ad.] To; at; on; -- in OF. shortened to a-. See Ad-. (c) The Arabic definite article answering to the English the; as, Alkoran, the Koran or the Book; alchemy, the chemistry.
allonymous: Published under the name of some one other than the author.
alter: 1. To make otherwise; to change in some respect, either partially or wholly; to vary; to modify. "To alter the king's course." "To alter the condition of a man." "No power in Venice can alter a… | To become, in some respects, different; to vary; to change; as, the weather alters almost daily; rocks or minerals alter by exposure. "The law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not." Dan. vi.
allatrate: To bark as a dog. (old) Stubbes.
aliquot: An aliquot part of a number or quantity is one which will divide it without a remainder; thus, 5 is an aliquot part of 15. Opposed to aliquant.
alphorn: A curved wooden horn about three feet long, with a cupped mouthpiece and a bell, used by the Swiss to sound the ranz des vaches and other melodies. Its notes are open harmonics of the tube.
aleppoboil: A chronic skin affection terminating in an ulcer, most commonly of the face. It is endemic along the Mediterranean, and is probably due to a specific bacillus. Called also Aleppo ulcer, Biskara boil, Delhi boil, Oriental sore, etc.
alexia: (a) As used by some, inability to read aloud, due to brain disease. (b) More commonly, inability, due to brain disease, to understand written or printed symbols although they can be seen, as in case of word blindness.
alderfly: 1. Any of numerous neuropterous insects of the genus Sialis or allied genera. They have aquatic larvæ, which are used for bait. 2. (Angling) An artificial fly with brown mottled wings, body of peacock harl, and black legs.
almshouse: A house appropriated for the use of the poor; a poorhouse.
allicient: That attracts; attracting. -- n. That attracts. [Rare or Obs.]
alfenide: An alloy of nickel and silver electroplated with silver.
align: To adjust or form to a line; to range or form in line; to bring into line; to aline. | To form in line; to fall into line.
allwork: Domestic or other work of all kinds; as, a maid of allwork, that is, a general servant.
alto: 1. (Mus.) Formerly the part sung by the highest male, or counter-tenor, voices; now the part sung by the lowest female, or contralto, voices, between in tenor and soprano. In instrumental music it now signifies the tenor. 2. An alto singer. Alto clef (Mus.) the counter-tenor clef, or the C clef, placed so that the two strokes include the middle line of the staff. Moore.
alkoran: The Mohammedan Scriptures. Same as Alcoran and Koran.
alkaliflat: A sterile plain, containing an excess of alkali, at the bottom of an undrained basin in an arid region; a playa.
aldermanly: Pertaining to, or like, an alderman. | Pertaining to, or like, an alderman. "An aldermanly discretion." Swift.
allantoidea: The division of Vertebrata in which the embryo develops an allantois. It includes reptiles, birds, and mammals.
allopathy: That system of medical practice which aims to combat disease by the use of remedies which produce effects different from those produced by the special disease treated; -- a term invented by Hahnemann to designate the ordinary practice, as opposed to homeopathy.
allotment: 1. The act of allotting; assignment. 2. That which is allotted; a share, part, or portion granted or distributed; that which is assigned by lot, or by the act of God; anything set apart for a special use or to a distinct party. The alloments of God and nature. L'Estrange. A vineyard and an allotment for olives and herbs. Broome. 3.
altostratus: A cloud formation similar to cirro-stratus, but heavier and at a lower level.
alumna: A female pupil; especially, a graduate of a school or college.
allegiance: 1. The tie or obligation, implied or expressed, which a subject owes to his sovereign or government; the duty of fidelity to one's king, government, or state. 2. Devotion; loyalty; as, allegiance to science. Syn. -- Loyalty; fealty. -- Allegiance, Loyalty.
alpine: 1. Of or pertaining to the Alps, or to any lofty mountain; as, Alpine snows; Alpine plants. 2. Like the Alps; lofty. "Gazing up an Alpine height." Tennyson.
alpenglow: A reddish glow seen near sunset or sunrise on the summits of mountains; specif., a reillumination sometimes observed after the summits have passed into shadow, supposed to be due to a curving downward (refraction) of the light rays from the west resulting from the cooling of the air.
alive: 1. Having life, in opposition to dead; living; being in a state in which the organs perform their functions; as, an animal or a plant which is alive. 2. In a state of action; in force or operation; unextinguished; unexpired; existent; as, to keep the fire alive; to keep the affections alive. 3. Exhibiting the activity and motion of many living beings; swarming; thronged.
albicore: A name applied to several large fishes of the Mackerel family, esp. Orcynus alalonga. One species (Orcynus thynnus), common in the Mediterranean and Atlantic, is called in New England the horse mackerel; the tunny. [Written also albacore.]
allnight: Light, fuel, or food for the whole night. (old) Bacon.
albigensian: Of or pertaining to the Albigenses.
albinoism: The state or condition of being an albino; albinism.
ally: 1. To unite, or form a connection between, as between families by marriage, or between princes and states by treaty, league, or confederacy; -- often followed by to or with. | 1. alcoometry: See Alcoholometry. Note: The chemists say alcomètre, alcoomètrie, doubtless by the suppression of a syllable in order to avoid a disagreeable sequence of sounds. (Cf. Idolatry.) Littré.
albion: An ancient name of England, still retained in poetry. In that nook-shotten isle of Albion. Shak.
alnage: Measurement (of cloth) by the ell; also, a duty for such measurement.
allhail: To salute; to greet. [Poet.] Whiles I stood rapt in the wonder of it, came missives from the king, who all-hailed me "Thane of Cawdor." Shak.
alula: A false or bastard wing. See under Bastard.
albumenize: To cover or saturate with albumen; to coat or treat with an albuminous solution; as, to albuminize paper.
albigeois: A sect of reformers opposed to the church of Rome in the 12th centuries. Note: The Albigenses were a branch of the Catharists (the pure). They were exterminated by crusades and the Inquisition. They were distinct from the Waldenses.
alum: A double sulphate formed of aluminium and some other element (esp. an alkali metal) or of aluminium. It has twenty-four molecules of water of crystallization. Note: Common alum is the double sulphate… | To steep in, or otherwise impregnate with, a solution of alum; to treat with alum. Ure.
alb: A vestment of white linen, reaching to the feet, an enveloping the person; -- in the Roman Catholic church, worn by those in holy orders when officiating at mass. It was formerly worn, at least by clerics, in daily life.
allegement: Allegation. (old) With many complaints and allegements. Bp. Sanderson.
alow: Below; in a lower part. "Aloft, and then alow." Dryden.
aleuromancy: Divination by means of flour. Encyc. Brit.
allotropism: The property of existing in two or more conditions which are distinct in their physical or chemical relations. alcooemetry: See Alcoholometry. Note: The chemists say alcomètre, alcoomètrie, doubtless by the suppression of a syllable in order to avoid a disagreeable sequence of sounds. (Cf. Idolatry.) Littré.
altaian: Of or pertaining to the Altai, a mountain chain in Central Asia.
albescent: Becoming white or whitish; moderately white.
alliciency: Attractive power; attractiveness. (old) Sir T. Browne.
albuminoid: Resembling albumin. -- n. One of a class of organic principles (called also proteids) which form the main part of organized tissues. Brunton.
allayment: An allaying; that which allays; mitigation. (old) The like allayment could I give my grief. Shak.
allhalloweve: The evening before Allhallows. See Halloween.
alcoholature: An alcoholic tincture prepared with fresh plants. New Eng. Dict.
alcarraza: A vessel of porous earthenware, used for cooling liquids by evaporation from the exterior surface.
alpharays: Rays of relatively low penetrating power emitted by radium and other radioactive substances, and shown to consist of positively charged particles (perhaps particles of helium) having enormous velocities but small masses. They are slightly deflected by a strong magnetic or electric field.
almadia: (a) A bark canoe used by the Africans. (b) A boat used at Calicut, in India, about eighty feet long, and six or seven broad.
aleutian: Of or pertaining to a chain of islands between Alaska and Kamtchatka; also, designating these islands.
altaic: Of or pertaining to the Altai, a mountain chain in Central Asia.
alienage: 1. The state or legal condition of being an alien. Note: The disabilities of alienage are removable by naturalization or by special license from the State of residence, and in some of the United States by declaration of intention of naturalization. Kent. Wharton. Estates forfeitable on account of alienage. Story. 2. The state of being alienated or transferred to another.
almsman: 1. A recipient of alms. Shak. 2. A giver of alms. Halliwell.
alfagrass: A plant (Macrochloa tenacissima) of North Africa; also, its fiber, used in paper making.
alcedo: A genus of perching birds, including the European kingfisher (Alcedo ispida). See Halcyon.
alligator: 1. (Zoöl.) A large carnivorous reptile of the Crocodile family, peculiar to America. It has a shorter and broader snout than the crocodile, and the large teeth of the lower jaw shut into pits in the upper jaw, which has no marginal notches. Besides the common species of the southern United States, there are allied species in South America. 2.

althaea: (a) A genus of plants of the Mallow family. It includes the officinal marsh mallow, and the garden hollyhocks. (b) An ornamental shrub (Hibiscus Syriacus) of the Mallow family.
alternant: Composed of alternate layers, as some rocks.
aleppoevil: A chronic skin affection terminating in an ulcer, most commonly of the face. It is endemic along the Mediterranean, and is probably due to a specific bacillus. Called also Aleppo ulcer, Biskara boil, Delhi boil, Oriental sore, etc.
alternity: Succession by turns; alternation. Sir T. Browne.
alimentiveness: The instinct or faculty of appetite for food. [Chiefly in Phrenol.]
altimeter: An instrument for taking altitudes, as a quadrant, sextant, etc. Knight.
allantoid: Of or pertaining to the allantois. | A membranous appendage of the embryos of mammals, birds, and reptiles, -- in mammals serving to connect the fetus with the parent; the urinary vesicle.
alcoholometry: The process or method of ascertaining the proportion of pure alcohol which spirituous liquors contain.
alluvial: Pertaining to, contained in, or composed of, alluvium; relating to the deposits made by flowing water; washed away from one place and deposited in another; as, alluvial soil, mud, accumulations, deposits.
allowableness: The quality of being allowable; permissibleness; lawfulness; exemption from prohibition or impropriety. South.
alchemy: 1. An imaginary art which aimed to transmute the baser metals into gold, to find the panacea, or universal remedy for diseases, etc. It led the way to modern chemistry. 2. A mixed metal composed mainly of brass, formerly used for various utensils; hence, a trumpet. (old) Put to their mouths the sounding alchemy. Milton. 3.
alimony: 1. Maintenance; means of living. 2. (Law) An allowance made to a wife out of her husband's estate or income for her support, upon her divorce or legal separation from him, or during a suit for the same. Wharton. Burrill.
alegge: To allay or alleviate; to lighten. (old) That shall alegge this bitter blast. Spenser.
alderney: One of a breed of cattle raised in Alderney, one of the Channel Islands. Alderneys are of a dun or tawny color and are often called Jersey cattle. See Jersey, 3.
alligation: 1. The act of tying together or attaching by some bond, or the state of being attached. 2. (Arith.) A rule relating to the solution of questions concerning the compounding or mixing of different ingredients, or ingredients of different qualities or values. Note: The rule is named from the method of connecting together the terms by certain ligature-like signs.
almighty: 1. Unlimited in might; omnipotent; all-powerful; irresistible. I am the Almighty God. Gen. xvii. 1. 2. Great; extreme; terrible. [Slang] Poor Aroar can not live, and can not die, -- so that he is in an almighty fix. De Quincey. The Almighty, the omnipotent God. Rev. i. 8.
alkalize: To render alkaline; to communicate the properties of an alkali to.
alcaldia: The jurisdiction or office of an alcalde; also, the building or chamber in which he conducts the business of his office.
alumnus: A pupil; especially, a graduate of a college or other seminary of learning.
alexiteric: A preservative against contagious and infectious diseases, and the effects of poison in general. Brande & C. | Resisting poison; obviating the effects of venom; alexipharmic.
algebraic: Of or pertaining to algebra; containing an operation of algebra, or deduced from such operation; as, algebraic characters; algebraical writings. Algebraic curve, a curve such that the equation which expresses the relation between the coördinates of its points involves only the ordinary operations of algebra; -- opposed to a transcendental curve.
allower: 1. An approver or abettor. (old) 2. One who allows or permits.
algarovilla: The agglutinated seeds and husks of the legumes of a South American tree (Inga Marthæ). It is valuable for tanning leather, and as a dye.
almightiness: Omnipotence; infinite or boundless power; unlimited might. Jer. Taylor.
allogamy: Fertilization of the pistil of a plant by pollen from another of the same species; cross-fertilization.
almost: Nearly; well nigh; all but; for the greatest part. Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian. Acts xxvi. 28. Almost never, scarcely ever. -- Almost nothing, scarcely anything.
allow: 1. To praise; to approve of; hence, to sanction. [Obs. or Archaic] Ye allow the deeds of your fathers. Luke xi. 48. We commend his pains, condemn his pride, allow his life, approve his learning. | To admit; to concede; to make allowance or abatement. Allowing still for the different ways of making it. Addison. To allow of, to permit; to admit. Shak.
aliped: Wing-footed, as the bat. -- n. An animal whose toes are connected by a membrane, serving for a wing, as the bat.
albugineous: Of the nature of, or resembling, the white of the eye, or of an egg; albuminous; -- a term applied to textures, humors, etc., which are perfectly white.
